content:
incident-bot: ALERT fired: redis-cluster-prod - clients_max_reached (severity: critical)
incident-bot: service: redis-prod-primary | trigger: maxclients reached on shard-03 | link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PDT12345
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PDT12345 triggered and paged rotation: oncall-eng (escalation: initial)
kevin: acked on PagerDuty — grabbing it now
dina: I'm nearby, can help with quick triage, handing off ops if needed
kevin: summary from alert: redis reporting 'maxclients' hit, new connections failing, client-side errors observed in API logs (ERR max number of clients reached)
ashley: seeing a spike in 5xxs for /v1/embed from Canary region, correlates with 12:10 UTC
michael: got the Grafana panel up — connections jumped from ~3.2k to 10k in ~2m on shard-03
sre-shiftlead: set severity P1 for now. Please record impact and mitigation steps as we go.
kevin: running quick redis INFO clients on shard-03
kevin: ```
# redis-cli -h shard-03.prod redis INFO clients
connected_clients:10002
blocked_clients:0
maxclients:10000
client_recent_max_output_buffer:0
```
dina: Oof, exactly at max. App pools are creating too many idle conns. Any backoff or leak?
kevin: grep logs for connection errors in API hosts - a few libs report reconnect loops. Sharing snippet:
kevin: ```
2026-03-14T12:09:58Z api-12 ERROR redis: dial tcp x.x.x.x:6379: connect: connection refused
2026-03-14T12:10:01Z api-12 WARN redis: reconnecting (retrying)
```
ashley: looks like a burst from bulk-embed job starting at 12:08 — we had a scheduled data-hydration job mistakenly enabled on prod Canary (my bad)
michael: that job opens hundreds of short-lived connections in parallel, our pool doesn't reuse them.
kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) block the offending job 2) increase redis maxclients 3) drop idle clients from app tier 4) failover to replica (risky)
dina: option 1 is fastest — where's the job? ashley, can you stop it?
ashley: stopping job now — disabling cron via jobs-service (running command)
ashley: ```
POST /internal/jobs/disable bulk-hydration-job-prod
response: 200 OK
```
kevin: nice, jobs-service returned 200. Waiting for connection pressure to fall.
sre-shiftlead: rollcall: kevin (primary), dina (secondary), michael (observability), ashley (app owner)
kevin: monitoring connections...
kevin: connections dropped to ~8200 after job kill, still above 7k
dina: app pools still holding many sockets — we can trigger a graceful driver restart on a subset of API nodes to free pooled sockets. We should stagger to avoid traffic blips.
michael: agree. I'll coordinate a 5-host rolling restart, 30s drain each.
kevin: also we can temporarily bump `maxclients` to 15000 for shard-03 via CONFIG SET — that'll avoid immediate rejections while we stabilize. Thoughts?
sre-shiftlead: CONFIG SET ok as short-term, but must be reverted and document risk. Need to check ulimit and memory headroom.
dina: checking redis memory: used 6.2GB of 16GB — headroom exists. ulimit for fd we need to confirm.
kevin: running: `CONFIG GET maxclients` returned 10000; setting to 15000 now
kevin: ```
redis-cli -h shard-03 CONFIG SET maxclients 15000
OK
```
kevin: clients accepted again, errors dropping from API logs
kevin: connections now at 9200 and falling
ashley: still seeing elevated 5xx in Canary but trending down. Notifying product customers?
customer-success-bot: Alert sent to CS channel with initial template — tagging customers with active sessions in Canary.
ashley: posting in #customer-impact with list and ETA to recover
kevin: starting rolling restart of API hosts in Canary fleet (5 hosts) — will do 1 at a time, 60s drain, 2m pause between hosts
dina: I'll watch for error spikes and abort if needed
michael: observability: latency on /generate is back to baseline in NA, Canary will follow after restarts.
kevin: after 3 restarts connections down to 4700, by end of rolling restart at ~12:40 UTC connections at ~2.1k
sre-shiftlead: nice work — update incident notes, root cause suspected: accidental scheduled job (bulk-hydration) in Canary causing parallel connection storm and driver reconnect loops -> connection leak behavior exacerbated by pool config
kevin: next actions: 1) revert maxclients to 10000 after 1h of stable metrics 2) postmortem ownership to ashley & platform infra 3) patch jobs-service to prevent prod-crons in Canary 4) add client-side connection pooling fixes and circuit-breaker
ashley: I'll own job config fixes and postmortem writeup, will link to this thread.
dina: I'll follow up on app driver changes (connection reuse) and add a test to simulate bulk job in staging.
michael: I'll add dashboard alert to warn at 70% of maxclients and a synthetic that runs job-shaped load.
sre-shiftlead: set P1 -> P2 in 1h if stable. Keep timeline and customer comms updated.
kevin: marking incident as stabilized, keeping PagerDuty incident open until we revert config and confirm no regression.
pagerduty-bot: Incident PDT12345 status: acknowledged -> monitoring.
kevin: recording impact: ~5–10% increase in 500s for certain embed endpoints in Canary; no major production customers affected in NA or EU.
customer-success-bot: CS notified customers on Canary and offered rollback steps for any affected.
ashley: creating follow-up ticket: INF-4538 - accidental-prod-cron-in-canary + action items
kevin: thanks all. I'll close the thread once maxclients is reverted and postmortem drafted.
kevin: last check 12:58 UTC — confirmed stable, connections under 3k on shard-03
sre-shiftlead: good. converting to monitoring state. Great coordination. :tada:
kevin: closing thread here, will update with postmortem link when ready
